source_text: Ἡσυχίαν μὲν λόγοις ἐπιτήδευε, ἡσυχίαν δὲ ἔργοις, ὡσαύτως δὲ ἐν γλώττῃ καὶ βαδίσματι· σφοδρότητα δὲ ἀπόφευγε προπετῆ· οὕτως γὰρ ὁ νοῦς διαμενεῖ βέβαιος, καὶ οὐχ ὑπὸ τῆς σφοδρότητος ταραχώδης γενόμενος ἀσθενὴς ἔσται καὶ βραχὺς περὶ φρόνησιν καὶ σκοτεινὸν ὁρῶν οὐδὲ ἡττηθήσεται μὲν γαστριμαργίας, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ ἐπιζέοντος θυμοῦ, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν, ἕτοιμον αὐτοῖς ἅρπαγμα προκείμενος. τὸν γὰρ νοῦν δεῖ τῶν παθῶν ἐπικρατεῖν ὑψηλὸν ἐπὶ ἡσύχου θρόνου καθήμενον ἀφορῶντα πρὸς θεόν. μηδὲν ὀξυχολίας ἀνάπλεος ἔσο περὶ ὀργάς, μηδὲ νωθρὸς ἐν λόγοις, μηδὲ ἐν βαδίσμασιν ὄκνου πεπληρωμένος, ἵνα σοι ῥυθμὸς ἀγαθὸς τὴν ἡσυχίαν κοσμῇ καὶ θειῶδές τι καὶ ἱερὸν τὸ σχῆμα φαίνηται. φυλάττου δὲ καὶ τῆς ὑπερηφανίας τὰ σύμβολα, σχῆμα ὑψαυχενοῦν καὶ κεφαλὴν ἐξηρμένην καὶ βῆμα ποδῶν ἁβρὸν καὶ μετέωρον.
thought_title: Calm in speech and movement, with the mind ruling the passions
orientation: Clement of Alexandria opens his instruction to the newly baptized by urging calmness in speech, action, and movement, so that the mind may remain steady and rule the passions.
pass_a_gloss: Practice calm in words, and calm in deeds, and likewise in tongue and in walking; and flee rash vehemence; for in this way the mind will remain steadfast, and not having become turbulent from the vehemence it will be weak and short in regard to prudence and seeing darkly, nor will it be overcome by gluttony, nor will it be overcome by boiling anger, nor will it be overcome by the other passions, lying exposed as a ready prey to them. For the mind must rule over the passions, seated high upon a quiet throne, looking toward God. Be not full of sharp temper in regard to angers, nor sluggish in words, nor filled with hesitation in walkings, so that a good rhythm may adorn your calm and the bearing may appear something divine and holy. Guard also against the signs of pride: a haughty-necked posture and a lifted head and a delicate and lofty step of the feet.

lemmas.gloss: will be overcome, will be defeated
prey, spoil, thing to be snatched
to rule over, to prevail over
being haughty-necked, holding the neck high

choices.why: The glossary requires 'calm' for this key term, denoting quiet self-possession in speech and action.
The glossary requires 'vehemence' for this term, denoting rash violent intensity that disturbs the mind.
The glossary requires 'mind' for this term, denoting the intellect that rules the passions.
The glossary requires 'gluttony' for this term, denoting ravenous appetite as a passion.
The glossary requires 'anger' for this term, denoting boiling hot temper as a passion.
The glossary requires 'pride' for this term, denoting arrogance shown in posture and walk.

pass_b_english: Cultivate calm in your words, and calm in your deeds, and in your tongue and your walk alike. Flee rash vehemence, for then your mind will remain steady. It will not become turbulent from vehemence and grow weak and small in understanding, seeing dimly. It will not be overcome by gluttony, but will be overcome by boiling anger and by the other passions, lying ready as easy prey for them. The mind must rule over the passions, seated high upon a quiet throne and looking toward God. Do not be full of sharp temper when anger comes, and do not be sluggish in your words or filled with hesitation in your walk, so that a good rhythm may adorn your calm and your bearing may appear godlike and holy. Guard also against the signs of pride: a haughty neck, a lifted head, and a delicate, lofty stride.

problems.quote: or overcome by boiling anger, or overcome by the other passions
problems.source_quote: ἡττηθήσεται δὲ ἐπιζέοντος θυμοῦ, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν
problems.why: English adds “not” changing Greek positive claim that the mind will be overcome by anger and other passions.
problems.fix: It will not be overcome by gluttony, but will be overcome by boiling anger and by the other passions, ready prey set before them.
problems.ruling: Greek ἡττηθήσεται δὲ is positive 'will be overcome'; English 'not...overcome' wrongly carries prior negation, reversing meaning.

edits.old: It will not be overcome by gluttony, or overcome by boiling anger, or overcome by the other passions, lying ready as easy prey for them.
edits.new: It will not be overcome by gluttony, but will be overcome by boiling anger and by the other passions, lying ready as easy prey for them.

fixed: The English added 'not' before 'overcome by boiling anger' and 'overcome by the other passions', but the Greek has no negation there: 'ἡττηθήσεται δὲ ἐπιζέοντος θυμοῦ, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν' means the mind will be overcome by anger and the other passions. Changed to 'but will be overcome by boiling anger and by the other passions'.

last_rejected.source_quote: οὐδὲ ἡττηθήσεται μὲν γαστριμαργίας, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ ἐπιζέοντος θυμοῦ, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν
last_rejected.why: Source says the mind will NOT be overcome by ANY of these; English says it WILL be overcome by anger and passions.
last_rejected.fix: It will not be overcome by gluttony, nor by boiling anger, nor by the other passions, lying ready as easy prey for them.
last_rejected.ruling: Greek: οὐδὲ ... ἡττηθήσεται γαστριμαργίας, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ ἐπιζέοντος θυμοῦ, ἡττηθήσεται δὲ τῶν ἄλλων παθῶν matches English contrast.
